visual_anchors.morphology_description: TALL TIERED CYLINDRICAL PHARMACY JAR. Approximately 7–8 horizontal bands alternating crimson-red and white/cream. Each band is separated by a narrow white rim line suggesting a segmented or multi-chamber vessel. The uppermost section is narrower (neck), topped by a small gold/tan finial or stopper ball. The base rests on a small footing ring. The bands are solid-filled with opaque crimson-red paint — NO liquid surface line visible inside, NO fill-level variation between chambers. The uniform solid banding strongly indicates DRY/SOLID contents (layered powder, dry herb, or pressed solid material). The lid appears sealed. No drip marks, no meniscus, no translucent wash suggesting liquid.
visual_anchors.state_of_matter: DRY / SOLID — opaque banded fill, no liquid level line, sealed lid, segmented chambers suggest dry powder or layered solid preparation

visual_anchors.morphology_description: SECOND TALL TIERED CYLINDRICAL PHARMACY JAR, positioned below the first in the left column. Nearly identical banded morphology — alternating crimson-red and white/cream horizontal bands. Slightly shorter overall. The lid ornament is more pronounced: a small flame-like or heart-shaped red protrusion at the apex (topknot), distinct from the ball finial of jar_upper_left. A small ring or collar separates lid from body. Base has a simple flat footing. Again NO liquid line visible, NO fill-level gradient — consistently opaque crimson bands from top to bottom. DRY/SOLID state confirmed.
visual_anchors.state_of_matter: DRY / SOLID — same banded opaque fill pattern as jar_upper_left, flame-topknot lid may indicate heat-processed or fire-dried preparation; no liquid indicators

visual_anchors.morphology_description: THIRD TALL TIERED CYLINDRICAL PHARMACY JAR, lowest in the left column. Same alternating red-white banded structure. KEY MORPHOLOGICAL DIFFERENCE: a DISTINCT GREEN PAINTED COLLAR or petal-like base ring separating the jar body from the foot. This green base element does not appear on jar_upper_left or jar_middle_left, constituting a visual differentiator. The base is flared/rounded in a slightly different profile. Lid appears similar to jar_upper_left (ball finial). Content bands: again opaque crimson — DRY/SOLID. The green base collar may indicate a botanical connection (herb-specific preparation) or a different ingredient category.
visual_anchors.state_of_matter: DRY / SOLID — opaque banded fill, but GREEN BASE COLLAR is a unique morphological marker possibly indicating herbal/plant-derived dry content or specific preparation category distinct from the upper two jars

visual_anchors.morphology_description: LARGE SINUOUS TUBEROUS ROOT lying in a horizontal snake-like curve across the upper-right zone of the page. The body is salmon-pink to red-orange, painted with a warm wash. The form undulates in two or three curves — distinctly reptilian or serpentine in character. At the left end (root base) a rounded bulb-head sits upright with a crown of small green starburst leaves. The root body tapers toward the right. The surface shows subtle red-line veining or striations. The root is shown ABOVE ground (not buried), suggesting it is a rhizome or aerial tuber being depicted in a harvested/prepared state.

BULBOUS ROOT WITH HANGING FIBROUS TENDRILS in the upper-center zone. A small rounded spherical bulb at top, with 4–6 long fibrous roots hanging downward like a root-beard. The entire specimen is pale cream/tan — very lightly pigmented, suggesting either a white-fleshed root (turnip-type) or deliberate colour coding for a different material state. The fibrous hanging roots are thin and organic, not stylized. No leaves shown.

The white-cream colour of the bulbs contrasts with the salmon colour of the upper root — these are consistently depicted as white-flesh roots (possibly allium or parsnip type).

container_label_grammar.finding: Three @Lc labels in f88v, all labeling morphologically identical tall-tiered red-and-white pharmacy jars. The locus type '@Lc' may stand for 'Label-Container' (not @Lp plant, not @Lf feature).

container_label_grammar.hypothesis: The suffix distinction '-d' vs '-m' vs '-dal' between three identical-looking jars containing visually identical dry solid contents may encode PROCESS rather than state. '-d' = standard dry preparation; '-m' = thermally processed (flame-lid jar); '-dal' = herbal/botanical-origin dry (green collar jar). This is a PROCESS GRAMMAR encoded in the @Lc suffix, not a state-of-matter grammar.
